english_title: Counterexample 2.1.6: A Nonzero Smooth Real Function Whose Zeros Are Dense on an Open Interval
statement_en: Consider $$f(x):=\begin{cases}e^{-1/x}&x>0\\0&x\leq0\end{cases}.$$ This is a smooth function because all derivatives at $x=0$ exist and are equal to $0$. However, on $\mathbb{R}$ its zeros are not isolated, so this shows that a nonzero smooth function need not have isolated zeros and therefore need not be real analytic.
key_techniques: flat smooth function at a point
callout_body: 考虑函数$$f(x):=\begin{cases}e^{-1/x}&x>0\\0&x\leq0\end{cases}$$这是一个光滑函数，因为函数$f$在$x=0$处任意阶可导，且导数为$0$但是显然函数在$\mathbb{R}$这个开区间上，零点并不是孤立的。从这里也可以反推，此函数一定不是$\mathbb{R}$上的实解析函数。
